steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat; stir in brown sugar and vanilla, then stir in oats. Cook over low heat until mixture is well blended, 2 to 3 minutes.
Press half oat mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan. Reserve remaining oat mixture for topping.

Meanwhile, melt chocolate chips and peanut butter in a small heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring frequently until smooth. Pour chocolate mixture over crust in the pan; spread evenly with a knife or the back of a spoon.
Crumble remaining oat mixture over chocolate layer, pressing down gently. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours or up to overnight. Bring to room temperature before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Bake Chocolate Oat Bars
raw_recipe.description: These yummy no-bake oatmeal bars with a chocolaty peanut butter layer are quick to make — you just need patience to let them set up in the fridge!

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make a quick dessert without even turning on the oven! A crust and crumbly topping made of oats, butter, sugar and vanilla and a center full of chocolate and peanut butter is the easiest recipe for deliciousness. Try drizzling the top with melted chocolate and a sprinkling of coconut or nuts.

review.reviewBody: What a great dessert! Took me only 15 minutes, start to finish. Very rich - a small bar goes a long way! The second time I made these, I followed some others' advice and increased the peanut butter to 3/4 cup (liked that change!), and decreased the butter to 1/2 cup. I didn't like the change to the butter - made the top too crumbly. I think next time I'll try 3/4 cup butter. Thanks for the recipe!

I took the advice of the former reviews and used a little less butter. I think that the longer you cook them in the pot the less greasy it will appear. I substituted 1/2 a cup of ground flax seed for the oatmeal to give it a more nutty nutritious flavour and substituted the peanut butter with butterscotch chips as there is always a risk of peanut allergies when serving to the public. Personally I would have preferred the peanut butter, but to be on the safe side. . . Nice and simple!

These reminded my husband of a cookie his late mom used to make him. He was SO happy that we found a similar recipe. These are his new favorite :)

In order to keep the oats from falling off, I cooked them much longer than the recipe calls for and I added a bit of milk. When the oats were nice and soft, I pressed the first half into the pan firmly, then after I added the chocolate I lightly pressed the oatmeal that goes on top into the chocolate. I had very minimal crumbling. Great quick recipe!

Excellent recipe. I made it with bittersweet chocolate and chunky peanut butter and it's absolutely delectable! Perhaps it would be better to cook the oatmeal a little longer, at least to the maximum time it says, for better results. However, now that I'm not allowed to bake, recipes like these are highly appreciated!
Delicious. They kind of crumbled when eaten but it was worth a hand under them! I used gluten free oats and they were wonderful AND gluten free!

I followed the advice of others and made some changes so I am only giving this 4 stars, but with the changes I made they are definitely 5 stars or better. I doubled the recipe and made in a 9x13 pan. I used 1 1/2 cups of butter instead of 2 cups. I think the bars would be very greasy with the full amount of butter. I also used 3 large Hershey's Special Dark chocolate bars instead of the chocolate chips. I made a sling out of parchment paper and lifted the bar out whole and cut it on a cutting board so it was very easy to cut the bars evenly. I cut them into very small bars since they are so rich. I made them for a reception at church and they were the cookie that everyone was talking about. At least 6 people asked for the recipe and one man who only knows how to microwave frozen dinners asked for the recipe so he could have his granddaughter make these bars for him. I will definitely be making these again.

After reading the reviews... I made some adjustments... Here's how i fixed the "crumbly", "bland", and "too much butter" problems. To fix the butter issue, I reduced the butter to 1/4c and subbed in 3/4c fat free plain yogurt. To fix the bland and crumbly problems i added about 2tsp of cinnamon, an extra 1/2tsp of vanilla, and 1/4c of honey. I tasted it before i spread in pan, pleased with both the flavor and texture, i then proceeded with the peanut butter chocolate mixture which i 1 1/2 times the recipe because thats just how i roll;) and i used dark chocolate chips and natural peanut butter (just personal preferences). And Viola!!! Delicious, not greasy, not crumbly. It was very quick and easy. I microwaved the chocolate/peanut and just poured it over the oat layers. Yes i said LAYERS! my top layer was chocolate! Yum!

Pretty good recipe. I added cinnamon and coconut oil to the crumble. I froze the bottom layer before adding the chocolate mix, then pressed the crumble on top and warmed the entire dish for a few minutes in a toaster oven to set everything before chilling over night. I'm always looking for oat and peanut butter recipes. This one worked well. Just a note for those who make major changes, then complain, should try to walk before they run.

This is great without changes except I did use less butter as others suggested from the start. On the second batch I decided to try making changes to the proportions of the layers . I increased the oats by 1/2 cup. I pulsed the oats in the blender once or twice to make them a bit finer before I added them to the butter. I also added a tsp. of salt. I love salty and sweet together and this was just my personal preference. I doubled the chocolate and peanut butter layer and used an 8X8 dish. They came out great.

I found the recipe to be easy to follow. I added a half teaspoon of cinnamon to the oatmeal/butter/sugar mixture. Additionally, I scattered half of the remaining 4 ounces of chocolate chips from the 12 ounce bag on the melted chocolate/peanut butter mixture and the other half on top of the final oatmeal layer. These turned out very enticing. They were easy to cut into bars once they sat out at room temperature for about 15 minutes. This is a keeper recipe!

Great tasting! I decreased the butter to 3/4 cup ( trying 1/2 cup next time). I used a 1/4 cup of honey instead of brown sugar. The big difference I did was toasting the rolled oats on the stove on low to medium heat. They didn't taste as raw.
I have this recipe in a Cookies cookbook. I ALWAYS double the chocolate and peanut butter. Come out great every time!!
Delicious and so easy. I use dark chocolate chips.
So good!
a definite keeper! I added extra oats and a little more chocolate chips and it came out delicious! I served it with some yogurt on the side. Will be making this again. Thanks!

Too funny... I posted this recipe on here back when I had dial up internet ( 1997-99) unfortunately I've had to make a new account a few years ago. I'd love to see what else I shared close to 30 years ago lol I just happen to be looking for it today to share with a friend cannot find my paper copy I started searching and here it is lol

Made this recipe as noted. I did have an excessive amount of chocolate/peanut butter goo left over, even after decorating the top of the pan. Also, after cooking oats in butter, as directed, there was a lot of butter still not absorbed. My tasting panel LOVED these treats! Will definitely bake the recipe again. And maybe add some crunchy salt to the top, and use less butter. (I just read the comments from years ago. Duh. A friend gave me the recipe and I researched it AFTER I made it)
I substituted Peanut Butter for Honey and added cranberries because I wanted it to be school friendly bar I send with my babies. Loved the fact it was super easy and no baking .
Love these! I added flaky salt and cinnamon!

I made this dish for a group of friends. I used almond butter instead of peanut butter. It was a little thicker than the photos but it was rich and creamy. I made the bottom too thick and I didn’t have enough oats to make it even on top, but I was still able to cover the pan completely. Next time, I will add a little bit more oats to the recipe.
